abstract: The 1.8-megadalton SAGA coactivator is organized into discrete functional modules, yet how individual catalytic modules are assembled and integrated into the holo-complex remains poorly understood. Here, we dissect the assembly pathway of the four-subunit histone H2B deubiquitinating (DUB) module in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Pairwise RIP-qPCR uncovers a unidirectional network of co-translational interactions sequentially linking Sus1, Sgf11, Ubp8, and Sgf73. Combining systematic deletion genetics with co-immunoprecipitation and quantitative NanoBiT assays in intact living cells, we demonstrate that these contacts form an obligate linear cascade rather than independent binary events: each upstream subcomplex licenses the next nascent-chain engagement, sustains downstream Sgf11 and Ubp8 stability, and precludes post-translational bypass. Conversely, DUB subunits exhibit no co-translational interactions with the SAGA core interface, indicating that completed modules dock post-translationally. Thus, unlike single-scaffold assembly models, SAGA separates multi-step co-translational module templating from post-translational holo-complex docking, safeguarding compositional fidelity.
